subject: Weekly fleet runway / Helios capacity ask — alignment & next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example.com>, rebecca@helios.ai
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2029 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly fleet runway / Helios capacity ask — alignment & next steps

Hi team + Rebecca,

Following up from yesterday's pipeline review: Helios wants to lock a committed pool for Q3 as part of DL-2026-089. They indicated a likely start in mid-July but want the option to scale at month boundaries. I attached their pipeline forecast and a draft of reserved capacity scenarios so we can map to fleet commitments.

Ask: can infra and finance run the three-tier commitment scenarios against our Q3 plan and confirm what we can guarantee (SLA/throughput) vs what we should expose as burst? Specifics we need:
- Guaranteed GPUs (count) for a 12-month commitment
- Typical per-token latency targets we can commit to in us-east-1
- Burst capacity headroom and expected cost uplift

Rebecca — can you confirm the minimum start date and whether Helios is expecting region constraints (they prefer us-east but mentioned eu-west as backup)? Also any procurement timeline?

I've copied Jordan/Ben/Laura to outline commercial next steps once infra confirms runway. Proposed timeline: internal alignment by Friday EOD, response to Helios by next Monday.

Attachments: helios_pipeline_forecast_q3.xlsx, reserved_capacity_scenarios.pdf

Thanks,

--
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example.com>, rebecca@helios.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2029 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly fleet runway / Helios capacity ask — alignment & next steps

Tessa — thanks for the context and the attachments. Quick take from infra after a first-pass sizing:

Summary (us-east-1 primary):
- Scenario A (conservative): 24 guaranteed A100-class GPU slots; burst up to +12 for short windows. Estimated additional infra headroom cost: ~12% on top of base commit.
- Scenario B (baseline): 40 guaranteed slots; burst +25. Cost uplift: ~22%.
- Scenario C (aggressive): 64 guaranteed slots; burst +40. Cost uplift: ~38%.

Notes and constraints:
- The runtime yields ~8–12 tokens/sec per A100 for the Helios QPS profile in our test harness; that becomes a useful SLA knob.
- If Helios requires region failover to eu-west, we need a mirrored reserved pool — effectively doubling the baseline guaranteed capacity cost unless we use cross-region burst routing.
- Lead time for reserving new dedicated pool capacity (procurement + infra provisioning) is ~6–8 weeks for A100-equivalent hardware in our standard dedicated offering. Can be accelerated to 3–4 weeks with burst credits and temporary spot-backed nodes, but that reduces SLA guarantees.

Action items for this thread:
1) Ben — run the revenue/discount sensitivity for 24/40/64 guaranteed slots and return TCO model (include burst uplift).
2) Laura — confirm whether we can accept a phased start (e.g., 24 guaranteed in July + scale to 40 by Sept) from a contracting perspective and how that affects billing dates.
3) Tessa/Jordan — confirm which scenario you want to present to Helios by Monday so I can lock provisioning timelines.

Attachment: reserved_capacity_scenarios.pdf (I exported the capacity curves and the provisioning windows).

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Infrastructure Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Rebecca Chen <rebecca@helios.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Apr 2029 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly fleet runway / Helios capacity ask — alignment & next steps

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications from Helios: 

- Minimum start date: July 15, 2029. We want the first committed pool available then.
- Preferred region: us-east-1. EU is backup but we'll only enable if the primary struggles.
- Target committed size: we can commit to Scenario B (40 slots) for 12 months if pricing is within the ranges Marcus mentioned. We would like the option to add +20 GPUs within month boundaries (i.e., burst contract clause).
- Procurement timeline: our PO needs to be issued by June 7 to hit July provisioning. We typically run a 30–45 day procurement window internally.

A couple of asks for the commercial note: can Redwood include a simple SLA paragraph that quantifies average per-token latency and a credit model if sustained latency exceeds targets? Also include a short description of the failover behavior if we need eu-west in a region outage.

We can sign off on Scenario B in principle but need finance to confirm dollar terms — Jordan/Ben, happy to loop in our procurement lead (procurement@artemisgames.com is cc'd here for cross-company coordination; she runs procurement for the Helios -> Artemis buying vehicle).

Best,
Rebecca Chen
Head of Product, Helios AI
rebecca@helios.ai
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.example.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example.com>, rebecca@helios.ai, procurement@artemisgames.com
Date: Fri, 19 Apr 2029 16:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly fleet runway / Helios capacity ask — alignment & next steps

Good notes everyone — consolidating next steps so we can respond clearly on Monday: 

1) Commercial stance: present Scenario B (40 guaranteed GPUs) with a burst clause permitting +20 within month boundary. Ben — please produce a short pricing sheet (list + committed discount + burst uplift) by EOD Monday.
2) SLA language: Marcus, can you draft the SLA paragraph that includes an average per-token latency target (we should give a realistic range based on your test harness) and a credit table tied to sustained latency misses? We can tweak wording with legal but we want something specific.
3) Phased provisioning: infra to confirm firm provisioning lead times if we land Scenario B by June 7 PO. Marcus — you mentioned 6–8 weeks; if procurement is June 7 that just meets a July 15 target but leaves little buffer. Please call out risk and any recommended mitigations (temporary burst-backed nodes, earlier partial delivery).
4) Docs & signatures: Tessa/Laura — I'll create the commercial terms doc in HubSpot (link below) and start the draft of the SOW. Once Ben confirms pricing, we'll route for signatures.

HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company/repo/deal/DL-2026-089
Drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleLink

I'll reply-all with a short, customer-facing summary once Ben and Marcus send their numbers (goal: Monday AM customer update).

--
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference
